core_obligations: Handle the proper case by the comparison map and its transitivity (proof lines 4456-4461).

Define mu_{f,K} by restricting the comparison map for a chosen compactification, and prove independence of the compactification by the sigma and tau diagram, the restriction lemmas and the identification alpha_g (proof lines 4463-4540).
Deduce the commutativity of the hexagon in the statement from the construction of the composition isomorphism and the transitivity lemma (proof lines 4542-4557).
proof_roadmap: Definition of mu through a compactification (proof lines 4463-4474).
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for a morphism f : X -> Y of FTS_S the lemma produces canonical maps mu_{f,K} : Lf^*K otimes^L f^!O_Y -> f^!K, functorial in K in D^+_QCoh(O_Y), and for a second morphism g : Y -> Z asserts the commutativity of the displayed hexagon relating mu_f, f^!mu_g and mu_{g o f} (statement lines 4426-4454). The proper case is disposed of by equation labelled equation-compare-with-pullback and, when g is proper as well, by Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback, which proves the commutativity in greater generality (proof lines 4456-4461). The map is then defined by choosing a compactification j : X -> Xbar of X over Y and restricting the comparison map L fbar^*K otimes^L a-bar(O_Y) -> a-bar(K) of equation labelled equation-compare-with-pullback to X, which is legitimate because f^! = j^* o a-bar (proof lines 4463-4474). Independence of the compactification is proved by the same strategy as Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-well-defined: for g : Xbar_1 -> Xbar_2 with g^{-1}(j_2(X)) = j_1(X), the two maps fit into a commutative diagram by Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback, and the maps sigma and tau restrict to isomorphisms over X by Lemma labelled lemma-compare-on-open; pulling back along j_1 and using the map gamma of equation labelled equation-sheafy together with Lemma labelled lemma-restriction-compare-with-pullback shows that both restrictions are the identity on j_2^*(...) and j_2^*a-bar_2(O_Y), which yields the commutative diagram asserting that the two constructions of mu_{f,K} agree under the identification alpha_g of the proof of Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-well-defined, after which the same categorical arguments show well definedness (proof lines 4476-4540; the author marks the last categorical step 'small detail omitted' and points at the lemma to mirror). The commutativity of the hexagon then follows from the construction of the isomorphism (g o f)^! -> f^! o g^! given in the first part of the proof of Lemma labelled lemma-upper-shriek-composition and from Lemma labelled lemma-transitivity-compare-with-pullback applied to Xbar -> Ybar -> Z (proof lines 4542-4557). Comparing the two compactification constructions through the gamma identifications, exactly as in the well definedness lemma for f^!, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
